sections.body: Intellectual property and trademark strategy in AI covers the legal work of securing, licensing, and enforcing rights in inventions, brands, datasets, model outputs, and synthetic media. In practice, AI tools now help attorneys and agents run clearance searches, classify goods and services, draft patent claims, review office actions, monitor infringing uses, and assemble evidence for enforcement. The work is not fully automated. A model can surface candidate prior art, flag similar marks, or generate claim language, but a human still decides what to file, what to license, and what to assert. The field also includes new questions about whether AI generated outputs can be owned, how likeness rights apply to synthetic assets, and how patent offices treat AI assisted inventions. These pages treat the strategy as a set of repeatable tasks, from search to filing to monitoring, rather than a single legal theory.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: The state of the work is uneven. Clearance searching and trademark filing have mature software support, with databases, classification tools, and docket alerts, but the final judgment remains with a qualified practitioner. Patent claim drafting is harder to automate because claim scope depends on the specification, prosecution history, and the law of the relevant jurisdiction. Infringement detection can scan marketplaces, social platforms, and model outputs at scale, yet it produces many false positives and cannot reliably determine substantial similarity or fair use. Licensing synthetic assets and likeness raises unresolved questions about consent, scope, and chain of title, and the answers vary by contract and by state law. The site tracks 146 active AI lawsuits, 92 of them intellectual property, and 29 AI case law precedents, which shows that courts are still building the rules rather than applying settled doctrine.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: The pages under this section follow the lifecycle of an IP matter. Prior Art and Clearance Searching is the entry point for freedom to operate and trademark availability, where a reader goes to understand search sources, query design, and risk scoring. Trademark Filing and Specimens covers the path from application to registration, including goods and services descriptions, specimen requirements, and office action responses. Licensing Synthetic Assets and Likeness addresses contracts for AI generated media, digital replicas, and persona rights, which is where a reader goes for deal terms and consent issues. Patent Claim Drafting explains how claims are structured, how AI tools assist with drafting, and where human review is still required. Infringement Detection and Enforcement closes the loop with monitoring, evidence collection, cease and desist practice, and litigation support, so the section shows IP strategy as a chain of decisions rather than a single filing.
